impact:
`zug backup` failed on every invocation against a Fly-backed install, so the documented way to snapshot the volume did not work at all.

MECHANISM: cmdBackup did fs.mkdirSync(backupDir) and then ran `fly sftp get -R /data/.zug <backupDir>`. fly sftp creates the destination itself and refuses to write to a path that already exists ("doesn't override existing files for safety"), so the pre-created directory guaranteed the failure. The failed run then left the empty dated directory behind, which made every subsequent attempt fail identically — including after a manual rmdir, since the next run recreated it.

A second backup on the same day would have failed for the same reason even without the bug.
resolution:
Only the ~/.zug-backup parent is created up front. The Fly branch leaves the dated leaf for fly sftp to create, appends a -HHMMSS suffix when the dated directory already exists so same-day backups work, and removes the directory on failure so a failed run cannot poison the next one. The local-copy branch still creates its destination, which `cp -r src/. dest` requires.

Verified by running it: 373 files, 1.9 MB extracted to ~/.zug-backup/2026-09-20-051934.
title: zug backup pre-creates its destination, which fly sftp refuses to write into — backup never worked
